ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: Ptolemaic Alexandria drew scholars such as Euclid, Eratosthenes and Herophilus to its Library and Mouseion.
The great royal library at the heart of Ptolemaic scholarship, whose reputation has shaped the ideal of a universal library ever since.
India's Golden Age produced Kalidasa's poetry and Aryabhata's astronomy, built on the place-value decimal system later transmitted to Europe.
From Baghdad, founded in 762, the Abbasids presided over a cosmopolitan court where al-Khwarizmi wrote his treatise on al-jabr.
The centre that translated Greek, Persian, Indian and Syriac texts into Arabic, preserving Aristotle, Euclid, Galen and Ptolemy.
Poet and mathematician who, under Seljuk patronage, produced the Jalali calendar of 1079, more accurate than the Julian calendar.
Song China issued state paper money from 1024, first recorded the gunpowder formula in 1044 and chose officials by written examination.
Rebuilt with the plunder of Timur's conquests, Samarkand became under Shah Rukh and Ulugh Beg a genuine centre of intellectual life.
Built in the 1420s, its tables listed more than a thousand stars and were later published at Oxford in 1665.
